key_insight: This paper argues that the main bottleneck in mega-scale reinforcement learning for robot control is not just compute, but the quality and balance of the training data. By using a more diverse and better-balanced reset/data strategy, robots can explore more effectively and learn complex behaviors with less task-specific engineering.
problem_solved: It addresses the exploration bottleneck in sim-to-real RL for general-purpose robots, where learning often depends on handcrafted rewards, demonstrations, and other per-task priors that are expensive to design and limit scalability.
method: Use massively parallel simulation to train robot policies at large scale.
Replace heavy reward shaping and demonstrations with diverse simulator resets to broaden exploration.
Balance the training data distribution so the policy sees a more useful mix of states and avoids getting stuck in narrow behavior patterns.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a simpler and more scalable path to robot learning: reduce manual reward engineering and rely more on data coverage and reset design. It can make sim-to-real RL more practical for many different robot skills, from locomotion to manipulation.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing massive simulation, diverse resets, and policy learning leading to real-world robot control.
A side-by-side comparison of traditional RL (shaped rewards/demos) vs. balanced data diet RL (reset-driven exploration).
A distribution chart illustrating how balanced resets widen the state coverage seen during training.
Icons for locomotion, grasping, and dexterous manipulation to convey general-purpose robot skills.
paper_title: A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Exploration Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control
paper_authors: Octi Zhang, Mateo Guaman Castro, Patrick Yin, Ignacio Dagnino, Abhishek Gupta
